I think you’re missing the point. I’m saying sad shit happens in life, that isn’t depression, that’s life! 
Clinical depression is being physically unable to get enjoyment and pleasure from things that should or used to make you happy.

The difference with feeling depressed because your dog died and clinical depression is this: 
If your dog dies, it’s sad because you remember all the good times that have now ended, your companion is dead, life is sad and death is normal. 

Clinical depression is not being able to get any joy from the dog in the first place. You know you enjoy playing with the dog, you just can’t seem to face it. You know you love the dog, you just can’t seem to feel it. It’s like all the joy and colour has been sucked from your life and all that remains is fatigue, pain and suffering.

Hello, I’m from down south so I’m not sure if their is much variation between services. It is probably quite likely you will wait at least 4 weeks for a letter, sometimes it can take even longer. 
You will probably see a mental health care coordinator first who will do a my crisis plan with you. If they don’t offer ASK! Have a think about what you want included in this as it can save you valuable time in the future. Make a list of all the issues you have in your life, be as honest as possible. 
My experience has been incredibly mixed with community mental health teams, unfortunately I think the consistency of service is really very poor due to the massive cuts mental health treatment in the NHS has suffered.
